Date: Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: Acme MAP: final hosting & region vote — acceptance checkpoint

Ellie / team —

Thanks for the quick sync last week. As discussed, attached is an updated Mutual Action Plan (Acme_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a short ops runbook (ops_runbook.pdf) showing the canary/rollback steps for each hosting mode. We want to lock hosting mode and primary region by end of next week so engineering can schedule capacity and procurement can scope contracts.

Quick proposal and asks:
- Decision window: choose one of Hosted | Dedicated | Private by EOD Thu 2027-04-08.
- Primary region: propose us-west for latency and existing peering; call out any regulatory constraints.
- Evaluation plan: 2-week functional PoC (feature parity + latency SLOs) then 1-week canary (10% traffic) for Dedicated/Private; Hosted option lowers time-to-live but requires data handling confirmation.
- Security checklist: Acme to confirm PHI handling requirements (if any) — I’ve CCed our delivery and legal leads.

If convenient, I propose a 30-min alignment call Wed 4/7 10:00 AM PT to walk through the MAP and finalize the vote. If you want to route questions to procurement/security first, happy to accommodate.

Attachments: Acme_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP), ops_runbook.pdf (canary/runbook)

Thanks —
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(d) 415-555-0132

Date: Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 10:05 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Acme MAP: final hosting & region vote — acceptance checkpoint

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the overview and the MAP. A few points from Acme side:

- Procurement note: we need a recommended default to speed contracting. Our procurement team leans toward Dedicated for predictable throughput, but they’ll need the SLA language you attached in the next version.
- Security note: our security folks flagged PHI considerations. If there’s any chance protected data will be processed, Private (on-prem/VPC with customer-managed KMS) is the conservative path. They asked for the security docs and a short memo comparing network isolation across the three modes.
- Region: us-west is preferred for latency but we must confirm data residency constraints with compliance.

I’ve attached our internal security summary (Acme_Security_Notes.docx) — it has redlines and a list of required attestations. Happy to join Wed at 10 if we can get a one-page tradeoff memo ahead of time covering: estimated time-to-production, expected cost delta, and rollback exposure by mode.

Ellie
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Duran <ellie.duran@acmehealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 2:30 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Acme MAP: final hosting & region vote — acceptance checkpoint

Ellie —

Appreciate the level-setting. I pulled together a concise tradeoff memo (summary below) so the Wed call can be focused on decisioning rather than education. I’ll drop the memo to the Drive and the HubSpot deal record: https://hubspot.com/deal/RWI-ACM-2027-042

Tradeoff summary (high-level):
- Hosted (fastest): Pros: fastest onboarding, lower upfront cost, Redwood-managed keys; Cons: additional compliance review for PHI, small migration effort if you later move to Dedicated/Private. ETA to PoC: ~3 business days.
- Dedicated (balanced): Pros: reserved GPU pools, stronger isolation, typical enterprise SLAs; Cons: longer lead time for capacity (2–3 weeks to provision committed pool), higher monthly commit. ETA to PoC: ~7–10 business days + canary week.
- Private (most conservative): Pros: full control (VPC/on-prem), KMS/HSM integration, fits strict PHI requirements; Cons: procurement + infra timeline (4–8 weeks), potential on-prem ops burden. ETA to PoC: ~4–8 weeks depending on on-prem readiness.

Cost delta (very rough): Hosted < Dedicated (~1.5–2x hosted on unit cost) < Private (depends on infra). We’ll provide detailed per-token estimates after we know expected QPS and average sequence lengths.

Next steps for Wed 4/7 call:
- We’ll present the one-page memo and targeted SLA snippet for Dedicated.
- Acme to indicate whether PHI will be in scope (security/procurement).
- If Acme confirms no PHI, recommend Dedicated us-west as the default to balance throughput and timeline. If PHI is in scope, recommend Private with a parallel Dedicated evaluation to keep production options open.

I’ve uploaded a one-pager and SLA draft to Drive and the DocuSign starter for procurement: https://drive.redwood.com/Acme/MAP/Acme_MAP_v2.xlsx

—Priyom
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acme MAP: final hosting & region vote — acceptance checkpoint

Ellie / team —

Recap from today’s alignment and confirmed path so we have a clear MAP checkpoint for procurement/legal/ops:

Decision (agreed): Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated) in us-west as primary lane with private peering and optional customer-managed KMS. This balances Acme’s throughput needs and time-to-production while keeping a private on-prem path open if compliance requires it.

Key dates (MAP timeline):
- 2027-04-12: Redwood delivers SLA_Dedicated_Proposal.pdf (attached) and finalized scope for procurement.
- 2027-04-19: Dedicated pool provisioning window opens (Redwood schedules capacity).
- 2027-04-26: 2-week functional PoC complete (feature parity + latency checks).
- 2027-05-10: Canary rollout (10% traffic) with rollback hooks; full production after canary sign-off.

Action items:
- Acme procurement: review SLA_Dedicated_Proposal.pdf and send redlines to procurement@redwood.com by 4/12.
- Acme security: confirm PHI-in-scope Y/N by 4/12 so we can finalize KMS and attestation language.
- Redwood: provide a one-page migration plan in Drive and the DocuSign starter (links below) to speed contracting.

Attachments: SLA_Dedicated_Proposal.pdf
Links: DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/documents/ACM-2027-042 | Drive MAP: https://drive.redwood.com/Acme/MAP
